title: You spend your day copy-pasting between two chats.
bullets: One thread per person. One chat per AI.
You carry the context between them, by hand.
illustration: Two chat windows side by side, the same message being dragged from one to the other. Build this one — no shoot needed.

title: Everyone works in one room — people and agents.
bullets: Several people. Several agents. One conversation.
Each on the app they already use.
An agent in the middle, sorting out who wants what.
illustration: THE money shot. The 4-up frame mid-conflict: Julie's phone, Tom's phone, the room view showing the agent's “Tom's villa is 16k, Julie's cap is 12k”, and the artifact.

title: You join by texting a bot.
bullets: Nothing to install. No account to share.
Phone, browser, or just reply to the email.
An agent joins the same way a person does.
illustration: One phone: “new” → the room code and QR come straight back. A second phone joins. Two real screens.

title: One orchestrator. N humans. N agents.
highlight: Only the orchestrator sees every thread — which is how it can tell you that what you just asked for contradicts what someone else asked for.

caption: The sandbox is the isolation boundary: nobody's laptop, and no member's credentials inside it. The room reaches the agent through the daemon; the agent reaches back out through one MCP tool, and only that one.

title: You are not the middleman anymore.
subtitle: Humans and agents, finally in the same room.

title: Eight findings, and where each fix landed.

findingsItems.label: a mid-turn prompt is lost without queue: true, and a killed session still answers 200 so resume reports success doing nothing
sandbox liveness unreported; orphaned boxes never reaped; a failed reconnect leaves the box running and billing
app serve ignores the declared UI path; a mutating proxy route had no auth gate
the fan-out cursor froze on resume, the artifact link outlived its box, and a recap fix shipped dead on arrival — each now has a regression test

highlight: Day one rule: never fork, never vendor, never patch the runtime. Eight findings later it held — seven pull requests open upstream, each with a test that reproduces the failure first.

title: On a real phone, in the rehearsal log.
bullets: Cold boot to a working room with a shared artifact: 86.5 seconds.
Two members on two surfaces, every message attributed, one reply reaching both.
The agent edits the shared artifact on request, confirmed live on its URL.
A PDF previewed, confirmed by a member, byte-matched in the inbox.
The sandbox deleted out from under the room — the next message revived it.
